parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.question_text:
Mechanical power P can be calculated using the formula P = Fv.
Use the concept of work and the definition of power to show how this formula is derived.
parts.question_text_latex:

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
The engine of a lorry provides 130 kW of power to the lorry’s wheels when it is travelling at a
constant speed of 25 m s^{-1} along a straight horizontal road.
Show that the resistive force opposing the forward motion of the lorry is 5200 N.
parts.question_text_latex:
The engine of a lorry provides 130 kW of power to the lorry’s wheels when it is travelling at a
constant speed of 25 m $s^{-1}$ along a straight horizontal road.
Show that the resistive force opposing the forward motion of the lorry is 5200 N.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
The lorry in (b) travels up a straight section of road that is inclined at an angle θ to the
horizontal, as shown in Fig. 3.1.
The lorry has mass m and the acceleration of free fall is g.
parts.question_text_latex:

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.question_text:
Determine an expression, in terms of m, g and θ, for the component of the weight of the
lorry that acts parallel to the surface of the road.
parts.question_text_latex:
Determine an expression, in terms of m, g and θ, for the component of the weight of the
lorry that acts parallel to the surface of the road.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.question_text:
The total resistive force remains unchanged at 5200 N and the engine now provides
greater power to maintain the speed of 25 m s^{-1}. The total mass m of the lorry is 36 000 kg.
The angle θ is 1.4°.
Determine the power, in kW, now provided by the engine.
power = kW
